title: Effects of Carnosine In Patients With Peripheral Arterial Disease Patients
official: Effects of Carnosine In Patients With Peripheral Arterial Disease Patients; Randomized Intervention Trial (CIPHER)
summary: The purpose of this study is to determine whether carnosine (a food ingredient found in chicken and red meat) supplementation (2 g) for 6 months in participants with non-claudication and claudication peripheral arterial disease (PAD) improves walking ability. Previous studies with heart failure patients have shown that carnosine supplementation increases walking capacity in these patients.
criteria:
Inclusion criteria

1. Participants between 40-80 yrs of age.
2. White or African American race, irrespective of Hispanic or non-Hispanic ethnicity Literate in English.
3. ABI \>0.4-\<0.90, obtained within 3 months from enrollment.
4. Willing and able to comply with protocol requirements.
5. Participant can provide informed consent.

Exclusion criteria

1. Participants with positive test for active Human Immunodeficiency (HIV), active chronic hepatitis B/C/T virus, significant liver disease characterized by ALT or AST\>3-5 times higher than the normal range, or total bilirubin \>3-5 times higher than the normal range, anemia having hemoglobin \<8.0 g/dL, end stage renal disease requiring chronic hemodialysis, or chronic renal replacement therapy, lung disease requiring home oxygen therapy, Parkinson disease that impairs walking ability, alcohol or drug abuse, increase in angina or angina at rest, end stage heart failure greater than class III NYHA, and active cancer will be excluded.
2. Critical limb ischemia with below or above the knee amputations or any form of leg ulceration over the symptomatic leg or using walking aid.
3. Presence of significant injury within 30 days and having an active or incompletely healed wounds, ulcers, gangrene, or vascular intervention on the symptomatic leg within 6 months before enrollment.
4. Participants with a baseline 6MWT of \< 122 meters (400ft) or \> 488 meters (1600ft).
5. Known allergy to L-carnosine.
6. Currently participating in other clinical trials.
7. Participants already taking carnosine.
8. Participants unable to provide urine sample (anuric).
9. Pregnant participants.
10. Participants using warfarin will not be included for biopsy.
11. Participants with MR incompatible internal metallic objects in body will not be eligible for MRI or 1HMRS.
